Subject: Hosted API integration architecture review - proposed times

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, I'd like to schedule a technical deep-dive with our engineering and SE team to review the hosted API integration for Finexa (SDKs, streaming, and tool/function calling). Proposed agenda (attached: finexa_arch_review_agenda.pdf):

- Quick intro & goals (10m)
- Hosted API overview + SDKs (15m)
- Streaming responses and handling partial outputs (20m)
- Tool/function calling patterns and security considerations (20m)
- Q&A and next steps (15m)

Proposed slots (PST):
- Thu Jul 30, 11:00–12:00
- Fri Jul 31, 09:00–10:00

If those don't work, please share 2–3 windows that do for you and any additional attendees (we'll make sure to include the right engineers). I've cc'd Aditya and Dev from our side.

Attachments: finexa_arch_review_agenda.pdf, redwood_hosted_api_quickstart.md

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the agenda. Thu Jul 30 at 11:00 PST is tight for us — could we do Fri Jul 31 at 10:00 PST instead? Also looping in Alex Gomez (our integration lead) — Alex will want to dive deeper into streaming behavior and function/tool calling for our orchestration layer.

A couple of asks in advance if possible:
- Can you confirm expected request concurrency and any guidance on batching for the hosted API?
- Will there be a short SDK demo (Node/Python)?

Apologies for the schedule churn — we have an internal review on Thu.

Thanks,

Hi Samantha / Alex —

Thanks for the note. A few items that will help make the session productive:

1) Expected concurrency (peak and steady)
2) Typical sequence length (avg and 95th percentile)
3) Which SDK(s) you'll use in production (Node / Python / Java)
4) Whether you'll rely on streaming clients for incremental UI updates or batch responses server-side

If you can share those before Fri Jul 31, I'll prepare targeted examples (code snippets) showing streaming socket handling, incremental delta parsing, and function-calling flow with security best practices.

Attaching a short network_requirements.xlsx that lists ports/egress expectations we typically need for hosted deployments.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
